newsitem.title: USA: Fort Howard Q1 to match, exceed Q4 results.
newsitem.headline: Fort Howard Q1 to match, exceed Q4 results.

text.p: Fort Howard Corp expects its 1997 first-quarter results to match or exceed those of the fourth quarter, said treasurer R. Michael Lempke.

For the full year, the Green Bay, Wis.-based paper products producer told analysts in a teleconference it is comfortable with the street earnings consensus of $2.35 a share, Lempke confirmed. "In fact, that (figure) may be a bit conservative," he added.
Before unusual and extraordinary items, Fort Howard reported earnings of $0.52 a share for the fourth quarter and $2.07 a share for the full year.
Fort Howard's fourth-quarter sales declined to $384.5 million from $415.3 million. For the year, sales were $1.58 billion compared to $1.62 billion in 1995.

"Tactical decisions were made in the fourth quarter to curtail sales (to outsiders) of jumbo unconverted rolls, a lower-margin business, in order to have necessary inventories to maximize growth over the next couple of years," Lempke said. The company slices the jumbo rolls, converting them into bath tissue, napkins and facial towels.
Fort Howard's stock was off 1-13/32 at 30-1/32.
